frequency.label: Contribution frequency
frequency.help: How often you add money. Contributing more often compounds sooner, so the result improves slightly.

chart.dragHint: Drag across the chart to see the total for a range.

interes-compuesto.title: Compound interest calculator
interes-compuesto.intro: See how much your money can grow by investing consistently.

help.initial: The money you start with today, before any contributions.
help.contribution: How much you add on each periodic contribution (based on the chosen frequency).
help.annualRate: The average annual return you expect. Global stocks have historically returned around 7% nominal, but it is not guaranteed.
help.years: How many years you stay invested. Time is the most powerful factor in compound interest.
help.annualFee: Annual product costs (a fund/ETF TER). They subtract from your net return. An index fund is usually around 0.1-0.4%.
help.contributionGrowth: If you raise your contribution each year (with inflation or salary), enter it here. Leave at 0 if fixed.
help.inflationRate: If set, you will see the final value in today purchasing power. Leave at 0 to reason in nominal euros.

independencia-financiera.title: Financial independence (FIRE) calculator
independencia-financiera.intro: Work out your FIRE number (the wealth to live off your assets) and how many years to get there.
independencia-financiera.notReached: Not reached within 60 years with these parameters

help.annualExpenses: How much you need to spend per year to live the way you want once financially independent.
help.currentSavings: The money you already have invested and that keeps growing.
help.savings: How much you save and invest each period until you reach FIRE.
help.annualReturn: Annual return after inflation (the 'real' return). Often estimated around 4-5%.
help.withdrawalRate: The percentage of your wealth you withdraw each year in retirement. The 4% rule (Trinity) is the prudent standard: a higher rate lowers the target but raises the risk of running out of money.
help.savingsGrowth: If you raise your contribution each year (with salary or inflation), enter it. Leave at 0 if fixed.

hipoteca-fija.title: Fixed-rate mortgage calculator
hipoteca-fija.intro: Calculate your monthly payment, total interest and how the outstanding balance evolves (French system).

help.principal: The amount the bank lends you (property price minus your down payment).
help.annualRate: The nominal annual interest rate of the loan. It does not include fees or insurance (that would be the APR).
help.years: Repayment term. More years means a lower monthly payment but more total interest.
help.openingFeeRate: Fee the bank charges at signing, as a % of the capital. Many mortgages now have it at 0.
help.annualInsurance: Annual cost of the linked insurance (home, life) the bank requires to grant the rate. Included in the APR.

interes-simple.title: Simple interest calculator
interes-simple.intro: Simple interest is always calculated on the initial capital, without reinvesting the interest. It is the typical model of a fixed-term deposit.
interes-simple.note: Indicative calculation. The tax withholding is an advance payment; the final tax depends on the rest of your savings income. Not financial advice.

help.principal: The money you invest at the start.
help.annualRate: The annual interest. With simple interest it is not reinvested: each year earns the same.
help.years: How many years you stay invested.
help.withholdingRate: Withholding on the interest. In Spain it is 19% for investment income.

deposito-plazo-fijo.title: Fixed-term deposit calculator
deposito-plazo-fijo.intro: Work out what you earn on a fixed-term deposit, after the Spanish withholding tax.

help.principal: The money you put into the deposit.
help.apr: The APR is the real annual return of the deposit.
help.years: How long the money stays locked. Decimals allowed (0.5 = 6 months).
help.withholdingRate: Withholding on the interest. In Spain it is 19% for investment income.
help.inflationRate: Estimated average annual inflation. Shows whether the deposit keeps your purchasing power. In Spain it is usually around 2-3%.

roi.title: ROI calculator
roi.intro: Calculate your return on investment (ROI), total and annualized, with costs, income received and taxes.
roi.note: Indicative calculation. The tax on the gain is estimated (savings tax base, 19%-30% in brackets); the real tax depends on the rest of your income. Not financial advice.

help.initial: What you invested at the start.
help.final: What it is worth or what you got back at the end.
help.years: If you enter it, we also compute the annualized ROI (CAGR).
help.costs: Buy/sell commissions and other transaction costs. They add to what you commit.
help.income: Income received during the investment (dividends, coupons, rent). It adds to your gain.
help.taxRate: Tax on the gain. In Spain capital gains are taxed in the savings base: 19% up to €6,000.

inflacion.title: Inflation (CPI) calculator
inflacion.intro: See how inflation erodes the purchasing power of your money over time.

help.amount: The amount whose evolution you want to see.
help.annualRate: Estimated average annual inflation. In Spain it is usually around 2-3%.
help.years: How many years into the future to project.
help.nominalReturn: Nominal annual return you place the money at. 0% = money sitting idle in the account. If it doesn't beat inflation, you still lose purchasing power.

cuenta-remunerada.title: High-yield account calculator
cuenta-remunerada.intro: Work out the return of a high-yield savings account, after the Spanish withholding tax.

help.balance: The money you keep in the account.
help.apr: The APR is the annual return of the account. It often changes over time.
help.years: How long you keep the balance. Decimals allowed (0.5 = 6 months).
help.withholdingRate: Withholding on the interest. In Spain it is 19%.
help.inflationRate: Estimated average annual inflation. Shows whether the account keeps your purchasing power. In Spain it is usually around 2-3%.

dividendos.title: Dividends calculator
dividendos.intro: Work out your annual dividend income and yield, after the Spanish withholding tax, and project the stream with annual growth.
dividendos.note: Indicative calculation. The withholding is an advance: dividends are taxed in the savings base (19%-30% in brackets). Not financial advice.

help.dividendPerShare: The annual dividend each share pays.
help.sharePrice: Current share price. Used to compute the dividend yield.
help.withholdingRate: Withholding on the dividends. In Spain it is 19%.
help.annualGrowth: How much you expect the dividend to rise each year. Many companies increase it over time. Leave at 0 if fixed.
help.years: Horizon over which we project and accumulate the net dividends.

staking.title: Staking calculator (crypto)
staking.intro: Work out the rewards of staking crypto assets, compounding at the APY, after the tax withholding.
staking.note: Indicative, high-risk calculation. The APY is not guaranteed and the asset price can fall. Rewards are taxed as savings income. Not financial advice.

help.principal: The amount you put into staking.
help.apy: The APY is the already-compounded annual yield. In crypto it can be very volatile and carries risk.
help.years: How many years you keep staking.
help.withholdingRate: Withholding on the rewards. In Spain they are taxed as savings income (19% by default).

promediar-acciones.title: Average price calculator (DCA)
promediar-acciones.intro: Work out the weighted average price of several purchases of the same asset, with commissions, and value the position at the current market price.

help.currentPrice: Current share price. Used to value the position and compute the unrealized gain or loss.

ahorro-jubilacion.title: Retirement savings calculator
ahorro-jubilacion.intro: Estimate the wealth you will have at retirement and the monthly income it could provide (4% rule).
ahorro-jubilacion.note: Indicative estimate: future return, inflation and fees are assumptions, not a guarantee. The 4% rule is a reference, not a certainty. This is not financial advice.

help.retirementAge: The age at which you want to stop working.
help.currentSavings: What you already have saved and invested for retirement.
help.monthlySavings: How much you save and invest each month until retirement.
help.annualReturn: NOMINAL annual return (before discounting inflation). For long-term equity index funds, 6-7% is a common estimate.
help.inflationRate: Estimated average annual inflation. Used to show your wealth in today's euros (real purchasing power). In Spain it is usually around 2-3%.
help.annualFee: Annual product fees (TER). They subtract from the return. An index fund is around 0.2-0.4%; an actively managed fund, over 1.5%.
help.contributionGrowth: If you raise your contribution each year (with your salary or inflation), enter it here. Leave it at 0 if it's fixed.

tarjeta-credito.title: Credit card interest calculator
tarjeta-credito.intro: See how long it takes to pay off a card debt and how much interest it costs you.
tarjeta-credito.never: With these settings the debt is never paid off: the payment doesn't even cover the interest. Increase the monthly payment (or, in revolving mode, the minimum payment floor).

help.balance: What you currently owe on the card.
help.annualRate: The card's annual interest. 'Revolving' cards are often 20% or more.
help.paymentMode: Fixed payment: you always pay the same. Minimum payment: you pay a % of the balance each month ('revolving' mode); as the balance falls so does the payment, so the debt drags on for years.
help.monthlyPayment: How much you pay each month. If it is too low, almost all goes to interest.
help.minPercent: The percentage of the balance the card requires as a minimum payment each month. Usually around 2-5%.
help.minFloor: The minimum payment amount in euros (the card never charges less than this). It's what stops the debt from lasting forever.

amortizacion-anticipada.title: Early repayment simulator
amortizacion-anticipada.intro: Put extra capital into your mortgage and compare the two options: lower the payment or shorten the term.

help.pendingPrincipal: The capital you still owe the bank.
help.annualRate: The annual interest rate of your mortgage.
help.remainingYears: How many years you have left on the mortgage.
help.extraPayment: The extra money you put toward repaying in one go.
help.compensationRate: Early-repayment fee the bank charges, as a % of the prepaid capital. The law caps it (e.g. 2% in the first 10 years on fixed-rate loans) and it's often 0.

presupuesto-mensual.title: Budget calculator (50/30/20)
presupuesto-mensual.intro: Organize your income with the 50/30/20 rule and find your savings rate.

help.income: What you earn per month after taxes.
help.needs: Essential spending: housing, food, utilities, transport… The rule suggests ~50%.
help.wants: Treats and leisure: eating out, subscriptions, travel… The rule suggests ~30%.

que-hipoteca-me-puedo-permitir.title: How much mortgage can I afford?
que-hipoteca-me-puedo-permitir.intro: Estimate the loan and home price you can take on based on your income and the effort rule.

help.netMonthlyIncome: What your household earns per month, after taxes.
help.monthlyDebts: Other monthly payments you already have (loans, car…).
help.downPayment: What you have saved for the down payment and purchase costs.
help.annualRate: The estimated annual interest rate of the mortgage.
help.termYears: The number of years over which you would repay the mortgage.
help.effortRatio: The share of your income that should at most go to the mortgage. The Bank of Spain recommends staying under 35%.
help.maxLtv: Share of the price the bank finances. Usually 80% (you need a 20% down payment).
help.purchaseCostsRate: Taxes and purchase costs (transfer tax/VAT, notary, registry…). Usually 10-12% of the price.

rentabilidad-alquiler.title: Rental yield calculator
rentabilidad-alquiler.intro: Work out the gross and net yield of buying a home to rent it out.

help.purchasePrice: What you pay for the property.
help.purchaseCosts: Taxes and purchase costs (transfer tax/VAT, notary, registry…). Usually 10-12% of the price.
help.monthlyRent: The rent you would charge each month.
help.vacancyRate: Allowance for empty or unpaid months, as a % of the year (5% ≈ half a month unpaid).
help.ibiAnnual: The annual property tax you pay to the town hall.
help.insuranceAnnual: Home insurance and, if you take it, rent-default insurance.
help.maintenanceAnnual: Expected repairs and maintenance per year (a common rule is ~1% of the price).

salario-bruto-neto.title: Gross to net salary calculator
salario-bruto-neto.intro: Estimate your net salary from your annual gross, deducting Social Security and income-tax withholding.
salario-bruto-neto.note: Indicative estimate using 2026 income-tax brackets, the personal and family minimum and Social Security contributions. It applies the state + supplementary regional scale: your region may change the result, as may other circumstances not covered here. Not tax advice.

help.grossAnnual: What your contract states before taxes and contributions.
help.payments: 12 payments = the extra prorated each month. 14 payments = two extra payments (summer and Christmas).
help.pensionContribution: Lowers the base on which income tax is computed. Maximum with relief: €1,500/year.
help.contractType: A temporary contract pays slightly more for unemployment (6.55% vs 6.50% for open-ended).
help.age: From age 65 the personal minimum rises, and more so from 75.
help.jointReturn: If you file as a family unit, a €3,400 reduction applies to the base.
help.children: Children or descendants you support. They raise the family minimum and lower income tax.
help.childrenUnder3: Each child under 3 adds an extra €2,800 to the family minimum.
help.ascendants: Parents or grandparents over 65 (or disabled) living with and supported by you.
help.disability: A recognised disability grade raises your personal minimum and lowers income tax.

irpf-nomina.title: Payroll income-tax withholding calculator
irpf-nomina.intro: Work out the income-tax percentage withheld from your monthly payslip and how much it adds up to per year.
irpf-nomina.note: Indicative estimate using 2026 income-tax brackets (state + supplementary regional scale). It approximates the tax agency's withholding algorithm from your salary, contract type and personal and family situation; your actual withholding may differ. Not tax advice.

help.grossAnnual: What your contract states before taxes and contributions.
help.payments: 12 payments = the extra prorated each month. 14 payments = two extra payments (summer and Christmas).
help.contractType: A temporary contract pays slightly more for unemployment (6.55% vs 6.50% for open-ended).
help.pensionContribution: Lowers the base on which withholding is computed. Maximum with relief: €1,500/year.
help.age: From age 65 the personal minimum rises, and more so from 75.
help.jointReturn: If you file as a family unit, a €3,400 reduction applies to the base.
help.children: Children or descendants you support. They raise the family minimum and lower withholding.
help.childrenUnder3: Each child under 3 adds an extra €2,800 to the family minimum.
help.ascendants: Parents or grandparents over 65 (or disabled) living with and supported by you.
help.disability: A recognised disability grade raises your personal minimum and lowers withholding.

irpf-autonomos.title: Self-employed income-tax calculator
irpf-autonomos.intro: Estimate a self-employed person's income tax under direct assessment from income, expenses and Social Security.
irpf-autonomos.note: Indicative estimate using 2026 income-tax brackets (state + supplementary regional scale). It applies the personal and family minimum. Under simplified direct assessment it includes the 5% hard-to-justify expenses (max €2,000/year); it excludes instalment payments. The real figure may differ. Not tax advice.

help.income: Total billed during the year for your activity (excluding VAT).
help.expenses: Deductible expenses for the year (utilities, supplies, accounting…), excluding your Social Security contribution.
help.socialSecurity: What you pay per year in self-employed Social Security contributions. It is deductible.
help.regime: Under simplified direct assessment you can deduct an extra 5% of net income for hard-to-justify expenses, up to €2,000/year.
help.pensionContribution: Lowers the base on which income tax is computed. Maximum with relief: €1,500/year.
help.age: From age 65 the personal minimum rises, and more so from 75.
help.jointReturn: If you file as a family unit, a €3,400 reduction applies to the base.
help.children: Children or descendants you support. They raise the family minimum and lower income tax.
help.childrenUnder3: Each child under 3 adds an extra €2,800 to the family minimum.
help.ascendants: Parents or grandparents over 65 (or disabled) living with and supported by you.
help.disability: A recognised disability grade raises your personal minimum and lowers income tax.

desgravacion-plan-pensiones.title: Pension plan tax relief calculator
desgravacion-plan-pensiones.intro: Find out how much income tax you save by contributing to a pension plan and the real cost of the contribution.
desgravacion-plan-pensiones.note: Indicative estimate using 2026 income-tax brackets (state + supplementary regional scale). Your individual contribution gets relief up to the lower of €1,500 and 30% of your net earned income. Employer contributions raise the joint limit to €10,000 but give you no direct income-tax saving (they are imputed as pay and deducted at the same time); their benefit is building wealth with tax deferral. Not tax advice.

help.grossAnnual: Used to place your marginal income-tax bracket, which determines the saving.
help.contribution: What you want to contribute this year. Only up to €1,500 (or 30% of your earned income) gets relief.
help.employerContribution: What your employer pays into a workplace plan. It lets you reach a joint limit of €10,000, but gives you no direct income-tax saving.

impuesto-patrimonio.title: Wealth tax calculator
impuesto-patrimonio.intro: Estimate your wealth-tax bill based on net wealth, the exempt minimum and your region's rebate.
impuesto-patrimonio.note: Indicative estimate using the 2026 supplementary state scale. Many regions rebate the bill almost to 100% or apply their own scale (e.g. Madrid). Adjust the exempt minimum and your region's rebate. Not tax advice.

help.totalWealth: Value of all your assets and rights minus your debts.
help.primaryResidenceValue: Your primary residence is exempt up to €300,000.
help.exemptMinimum: Amount that is not taxed. The state figure is €700,000, but it varies by region.
help.regionalRebate: Percentage of the bill your region rebates. Madrid, for instance, is around 100%.

impuesto-donaciones.title: Gift tax calculator
impuesto-donaciones.intro: Estimate gift tax based on the amount given, the kinship and your region's rebate.
impuesto-donaciones.note: Gift tax is devolved to the regions, which apply large rebates and reductions of their own. This estimate uses the 2026 supplementary state scale and the multiplier coefficient by kinship and pre-existing wealth (art. 22 Act 29/1987); it does not apply the «error de salto» adjustment. The real figure depends decisively on your region. Adjust the reduction and the rebate. Not tax advice.
impuesto-donaciones.kinshipI_II: Spouse, children, parents (Groups I and II)

help.amount: Money or value of the assets being gifted.
help.reduction: Reductions your region grants based on kinship. Leave it at 0 if unsure.
help.kinship: Sets the multiplier coefficient on the bill. The more distant the kinship, the more you pay.
help.preexistingWealth: Wealth the recipient already holds. From €402,678.11 it raises the multiplier coefficient.
help.regionalRebate: Percentage of the bill your region rebates. In some it is around 99%.

rentabilidad-alquiler-vacacional.title: Holiday rental yield calculator
rentabilidad-alquiler-vacacional.intro: Work out the yield of a short-term rental by occupied nights, after management fees and costs.

help.purchasePrice: What you pay for the property.
help.purchaseCosts: Taxes and purchase costs (transfer tax/VAT, notary, registry…). Usually 10-12% of the price.
help.nightlyRate: Average price you charge per night.
help.occupiedNights: How many nights a year you expect it rented (max 365).
help.managementRate: Platform or manager fee on income (Airbnb, Booking, local manager…).
help.cleaningFee: What the cleaning costs after each stay.
help.avgStayNights: Average nights per booking. Used to estimate how many cleanings per year (nights ÷ average stay).
help.annualExpenses: Fixed yearly costs: property tax, community fees, insurance, utilities, maintenance…

hipoteca-vs-alquiler.title: Buy vs rent calculator
hipoteca-vs-alquiler.intro: Compare the net cost of buying with a mortgage versus renting over a chosen time horizon.
hipoteca-vs-alquiler.note: The model invests your down payment (at the given return) in the renting scenario, but it does not reinvest the month-to-month cash-flow difference between the mortgage payment and the rent. If one option leaves you more free cash each month, its real outcome may be better than shown here.
hipoteca-vs-alquiler.sellingCostsRate: Selling costs at the end (% of value)
hipoteca-vs-alquiler.verdict: {option} is cheaper: you save about {amount} over {years} years.
hipoteca-vs-alquiler.verdictTie: Buying and renting come out about the same over this horizon.
hipoteca-vs-alquiler.buyEquityEnd: Net equity if you sell at the end

help.purchasePrice: Price of the home you would buy.
help.purchaseCosts: Taxes and purchase costs (transfer tax/VAT, notary, registry…). Usually 10-12% of the price.
help.downPayment: Capital you put down upfront. The rest is financed with a mortgage.
help.mortgageRate: Annual nominal rate of the mortgage.
help.mortgageTerm: Years over which you repay the mortgage.
help.annualCostRate: Property tax, community fees, insurance and maintenance per year, as % of price (around 1%).
help.appreciationRate: How much you expect the home to appreciate each year. A key assumption.
help.monthlyRent: What you would pay to rent an equivalent home.
help.rentGrowthRate: How much the rent rises each year.
help.investmentReturn: Return on investing the down-payment money if you rented instead of buying.
help.horizonYears: How many years you compare the two options over.
help.sellingCostsRate: Cost of selling at the end (agency, municipal capital-gains tax…), as % of value. Reduces the equity you recover if you sell.

salud-financiera.title: Financial health test
salud-financiera.intro: Answer eight questions and get a 0-100 score on the state of your finances, with tailored tips.

emergencyFund.label: How much have you saved for emergencies?

savingsRate.label: What share of your income do you save each month?
savingsRate.o0: Nothing, or I spend more than I earn

debt.label: What is your debt like (excluding the mortgage)?

housingCost.label: How much of your income goes on housing?

investing.label: Do you invest your savings?
investing.o0: No, everything sits in my current account

retirement.label: Are you preparing for retirement?
retirement.o0: No, I haven't thought about it
retirement.o1: I'll only have the public pension
retirement.o2: I contribute a bit now and then
retirement.o3: I have a plan and contribute regularly

protection.label: How protected are you against a serious setback?
protection.o2: I have some key cover (home, health…)
protection.o3: Well covered (health, home and, if others depend on me, life)

tracking.label: Do you keep track of your income and spending?
tracking.o0: I have no idea where my money goes
tracking.o1: A rough idea, nothing written down
tracking.o2: I check my accounts now and then
tracking.o3: I keep a budget and review it every month

advice.critical: Your situation is delicate and very exposed to any setback. In order: cut expensive debt (cards, revolving), gather a first €1,000 buffer and start tracking where your money goes. One step at a time.
advice.fragile: You have the basics, but an unexpected blow would knock you off balance. Build your emergency fund up to 3-6 months of expenses, push your savings rate toward 20% and automate saving on payday.
advice.stable: Good base. Now it's time to optimise: invest regularly and diversified (index funds), plan for retirement beyond the public pension, and check you're properly insured.
advice.strong: Your finances are very healthy. Focus on tax efficiency (pension plans, capital gains), keeping a diversified long-term portfolio, and aligning your money with your life goals.
